name: EARN RCT VoI BOTEC [2024]
summary: Funds a randomized trial (EARN) to learn whether a program is worth funding at scale. GiveWell's spreadsheet "EARN RCT VoI BOTEC [2024]", linked from its grant page. Every number is traced from the sheet's bottom line; calculated rows reproduce the sheet's own values.

rows.explainer: Because we currently estimate that this program is highly cost-effective (11-15x), it's more than likely that we would fund some amount of implementation without a trial. However, due to our high uncertainty about the effects of eyeglasses on consumption for a more general population (i.e. not only those in visionally-intensive occupations), we think it is unlikely that we would put a lot of money towards eyeglasses without additional trial evidence (particularly when our funding bar is 10x+).

rows.explainer: Assumption. This is based on forecasted funds raised.

rows.label: Weighted cost-effectiveness from value of information and program itself (x cash)
Risk that we learn this is above/below our bar and are wrong
rows.explainer: Assumption. This captures the possibility that we: (i) draw a noisy/biased treatment effect from the trial, (ii) update our funding decisions according to the trial, (iii) make the wrong ex post decision as a result.

rows.label: Risk that pilot/study is funded without us in a few years
rows.explainer: Assumption. This could vary based on likelihood of funging for specific pilot/trial. We shouldn't be assuming trial would never be funded

rows.label: Benefit from influencing other funders/value to broader research community
rows.explainer: Assumption. This parameter captures the idea that the trial we fund could update the funding decisions of other grantmakers/policymakers as well as our own.

rows.label: Total downside adjustment
Cost-effectiveness (x cash)
Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this grant's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers and advisers could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
